CREATE TABLE `bp_notifications`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `item_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `secondary_item_id` BIGINT NULL,
    `component_name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `component_action` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `date_notified` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `is_new` BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);







CREATE TABLE `bp_notifications_meta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `notification_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`notification_id`) REFERENCES `bp_notifications`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_activity`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `component` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `action` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `content` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `primary_link` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `item_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `secondary_item_id` BIGINT NULL,
    `date_recorded` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `hide_sitewide` BOOLEAN NULL,
    `mptt_left` INT NOT NULL,
    `mptt_right` INT NOT NULL,
    `is_spam` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);










CREATE TABLE `bp_activity_meta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `activity_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`activity_id`) REFERENCES `bp_activity`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_friends`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `initiator_user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `friend_user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `is_confirmed` BOOLEAN NULL,
    `is_limited` BOOLEAN NULL,
    `date_created` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`initiator_user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`friend_user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_groups`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `creator_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `slug` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `description` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `status` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `parent_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `enable_forum` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `date_created` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`parent_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`creator_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);



CREATE TABLE `bp_groups_members`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `group_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `inviter_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `is_admin` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `is_mod` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `user_title` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `date_modified` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `comments` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `is_confirmed` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `is_banned` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `invite_sent` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`inviter_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`group_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups`(`id`)
);






CREATE TABLE `bp_groups_groupmeta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `group_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`group_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_messages`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `thread_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `sender_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `subject` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `message` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `date_sent` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`sender_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_recipients`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `thread_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `unread_count` INT NOT NULL,
    `sender_only` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `is_deleted` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);





CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_notices`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `subject` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `message` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `date_sent` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `is_active` TINYINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_meta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `message_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`message_id`) REFERENCES `bp_messages_messages`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_groups`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `description` MEDIUMTEXT NOT NULL,
    `group_order` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `can_delete` TINYINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_fields`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `group_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `parent_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `description` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `is_required` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `is_default_option` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `field_order` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `option_order` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `order_by` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `can_delete` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`parent_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_fields`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`group_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups`(`id`)
);





CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_data`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `field_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `value` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `last_updated` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`field_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_fields`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_meta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `object_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `object_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`object_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_data`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`object_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_fields`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_user_blogs`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `blog_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_user_blogs_blogmeta`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `blog_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `meta_key` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `meta_value` LONGTEXT NULL
);


CREATE TABLE `bp_invitations`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `inviter_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `invitee_email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `class` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `item_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
    `secondary_item_id` BIGINT NULL,
    `type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `content` LONGTEXT NULL,
    `date_modified` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `invite_sent` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `accepted` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`inviter_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users`(`id`)
);









CREATE TABLE `wp_users`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
);

1) Background / Context
BuddyPress is a powerful social networking plugin designed to extend WordPress websites into comprehensive online communities. It is developed and maintained by Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com. BuddyPress provides essential components typical of online social networks, enabling features beyond standard blogging, such as user profiles, activity streams, groups, messaging, and more. 

 2) Objectives
The objective of BuddyPress is to enhance WordPress sites by offering a flexible framework for creating a wide range of community types. It is intended for use in various scenarios, including educational campuses, internal corporate communications, niche interest groups, product-focused communities, and integration with community forums via bbPress.

 3) Stakeholders & Users
- Website Administrators: Responsible for plugin management and configuration.
- End Users: Members of the online community who interact with social features like messaging, groups, and profiles.
- Developers: Those extending or customizing the BuddyPress functionalities for specific needs.

 4) Functional Descriptions
- User Profiles: Allow users to create detailed personal profiles with custom profile fields and visibility settings.
- Account Settings: Enable users to manage personal account settings, including email notifications.
- Groups: Users can create or join groups, forming micro-communities within the site.
- Activity Streams: Facilitate communication through real-time activity streams for members and groups, with sitewide directories.
- Notifications: Deliver smart notifications for various activities and interactions.
- Friendships: Support establishing and managing friendship connections between users.
- Private Messaging: Provide functionality for private conversations between multiple members.

 5) Non-Functional Descriptions
- Scalability: The system should efficiently handle increasing numbers of users as community size grows.
- Integration: Ability to integrate seamlessly with existing WordPress and bbPress installations.
- Usability: Intuitive user interface and navigation to ensure a smooth user experience.
- Security: Ensure secure handling of user data and communications, particularly with messaging features.
- Performance: Maintain responsive loading times and real-time updates for activity streams and notifications.

The database schema named "schemabench_0079" consists of 20 tables. The database is used for managing various aspects of a social networking platform, including user notifications, activity updates, friend connections, group management, private messages, user profiles, and invitations.
The "bp_notifications" table is used to store user notifications, including the user who generated the notification, the item associated with the notification, the component that generated the notification, the date and time of the notification, and whether the notification is new. The "bp_notifications_meta" table stores metadata related to these notifications.
The "bp_activity" table is used to store user activity updates, including the user who generated the activity, the component that generated the activity, the type of activity, the action performed, the content of the activity, the primary link associated with the activity, the item and secondary item associated with the activity, the date and time of the activity, and whether the activity should be hidden site-wide. The "bp_activity_meta" table stores metadata related to these activity updates.
The "bp_friends" table is used to store friend connections between users, including the initiator of the connection, the friend, whether the connection is confirmed, and the date and time of the connection. The "bp_groups" table is used to store groups, including the creator of the group, the name, slug, description, status, parent group, and whether a forum is enabled in the group, and the date and time of creation. The "bp_groups_members" table stores membership information for users in these groups, including the group, the user, the inviter, the user's role in the group, the user's title, the date and time of modification, comments, confirmation status, ban status, and whether an invite has been sent. The "bp_groups_groupmeta" table stores metadata related to these groups.
The "bp_messages_messages" table is used to store private messages, including the thread ID, the sender, the subject, the message, and the date and time of sending. The "bp_messages_recipients" table stores recipient information for these messages, including the user, the thread, the unread count, whether the message is only for the sender, and whether it has been deleted. The "bp_messages_notices" table stores notice messages, including the subject, the message, the date and time of sending, and whether it is active. The "bp_messages_meta" table stores metadata related to these notice messages.
The "bp_xprofile_groups" table is used to store profile field groups, including the name, description, and order of the group. The "bp_xprofile_fields" table stores profile fields, including the group, parent field, type, name, description, whether it is required, whether it is the default option, the order of the field within the group, the order of the option within the field, the method of ordering, and whether it can be deleted. The "bp_xprofile_data" table stores data for these fields, including the field, user, value, and the date and time of the last update. The "bp_xprofile_meta" table stores metadata related to these fields.
The "bp_user_blogs" table is used to store user blogs, including the user and blog. The "bp_user_blogs_blogmeta" table stores metadata related to these blogs.
The "bp_invitations" table is used to store invitations, including the user who sent the invitation, the inviter, the invitee email, the class, the item and secondary item associated with the invitation, the type of invitation, the content of the invitation, the date and time of modification, whether the invitation has been sent, and whether it has been accepted.
Finally, the "wp_users" table is used to store WordPress users, including their ID.
